ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $AB\parallel CD$, $AD\parallel BC$, $\angle DCE=90^\circ$, point E is on segment AB, $\angle FCG=90^\circ$, point F is on line AD, $\angle AHG=90^\circ$. If $\angle ECF=25^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle BCD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle ECF=25^\circ$ and $\angle DCE=90^\circ$,

$\therefore \angle FCD=65^\circ$. Also, since $\angle BCF=90^\circ$,

$\therefore \angle BCD=65^\circ+90^\circ=\boxed{155^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, AB and CD are two inclined parallel sides, AD is the upper horizontal line segment, BC is the lower horizontal line segment and extends to the right to G; point E is on AB, point F is on AD, the line segment from C to F is vertical, and B, C, G are on the same straight line. Observing with C as the vertex, ray CE is in the upper left, ray CF is upward, ray CD is in the upper right; CF is located between CE and CD. Reasoning: It is known that ∠DCE=90°, and ∠ECF=25°, so ∠FCD=90°−25°=65°. Also because in the figure B, C, G are collinear, and it is known that ∠FCG=90°, CF is perpendicular to line BCG, hence ∠BCF=90°. When measuring ∠BCD, ray CF is located between CB and CD, therefore ∠BCD=∠BCF+∠FCD=90°+65°=155°.
